Recall the following special limit: 

$$
{e}^{u}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{u}{n})}^{n}
$$

Hence, with $u=2y$, we get

$$
{e}^{2y}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{2y}{n})}^{n}
$$

Now, we rewrite the given limit using the algebra of limits, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{2y}{n})}^{n/2} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{[{(1+\frac{2y}{n})}^{n}]}^{1/2} \\  & ={[{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(1+\frac{2y}{n})}^{n}]}^{1/2} \\  & ={({e}^{2y})}^{1/2} \\  & ={e}^{2y/2} \\  & ={e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$
